source.title: Practical ICT Strategies — 7th Edition
source.integration_note: Structured summary for AEGIS. Preserve distinction between source claims and engine interpretation. Do not treat the book's causal claims as independently verified market facts.

source_claims: The book frames price as being delivered to seek liquidity and rebalance imbalance.
Recurring conceptual loop: seek liquidity, sweep, displace, rebalance.
Swing hierarchy uses STH/ITH/LTH and STL/ITL/LTL.
Bullish structure remains intact until a close below the most recent LTL; bearish until a close above the most recent LTH.
MSS is a displacement break of a relevant swing against trend.
CISD uses candle delivery and can occur before MSS.
MSS/CISD are triggers, not standalone strategies.
MSS following a liquidity sweep is presented as higher quality.
Displacement is forceful one-directional movement.
The book requires meaningful displacement for a valid FVG.
FVG is a three-candle imbalance and can act as entry location or rebalance target.
A dealing range is split at 50% equilibrium.
Above equilibrium is premium; below is discount.
Bullish bias seeks buys in discount; bearish bias seeks sells in premium.
OTE is 0.62-0.79 with 0.705 sweet spot.
Consequent Encroachment is the 50% midpoint of a gap/array.
BSL rests above old highs; SSL rests below old lows.
Important pools include previous day/week highs/lows, equal highs/lows, and obvious swing extremes.
A sweep takes liquidity then reverses; a run takes liquidity and continues.
ERL is range-edge liquidity; IRL is internal liquidity/inefficiency.
The book uses ERL→IRL→ERL as a recurring delivery concept.
Order Block: last opposing candle before displacement.
Breaker: failed OB after a liquidity sweep.
Mitigation Block: failed OB without a liquidity sweep.
Rejection Block: wick-based zone after a swept extreme.
Propulsion Block: candle that trades into an OB then launches price.
Hidden OB: overlapping-wick zone between two same-color candles.
SIBI is bearish FVG; BISI is bullish FVG.
IFVG is a failed FVG that flips and is retested from the opposite side.
Implied FVG is a hidden imbalance derived from surrounding wicks.
BPR is overlap of opposing FVGs.
Volume Imbalance is a body-to-body gap with wick overlap allowed.
Suspension Block is a candle suspended between two volume imbalances.
Vacuum Block is an opening gap from a high-volatility event.
The book prioritizes plain FVG and IFVG over collecting many gap variants.
The book treats time as a filter for delivery.
Asian, London, New York, and London Close killzones are emphasized.
Asian range high/low become later-session liquidity references.
CBDR is used for projection.
Macros are short timing windows around the hour.
NWOG and NDOG are opening-gap references.
Start high and work down.
Compare Daily↔H4, H4↔H1, H1↔15m.
Higher-timeframe context takes precedence.
Complete routine: Bias → Location → Draw → Level → Time → Trigger.
If a required step is missing, pass.
Use the most recent Daily MSS as the basic directional bias.
MSS up = bullish; MSS down = bearish.
Bullish bias seeks discount PD arrays and upside liquidity; bearish seeks premium PD arrays and downside liquidity.
The chapter instructs Daily-bias confirmation no lower than 15m.

ote.interpretation: precision entry-location model, not directional narrative

rules: identify last opposing candle before displacement
wait for sweep of obvious high/low
prefer no clean body close beyond range

silver_bullet.summary: One-hour, time-based FVG scalp with three daily windows.

judas_swing.summary: False initial move against the intended distribution; later integrated into AMD/Power of 3.

rules: bullish day manipulates down then distributes up
bearish day manipulates up then distributes down

unicorn_smt.unicorn: overlap of a breaker block and an FVG
unicorn_smt.smt: correlated assets fail to confirm one another

market_maker_models.summary: Market Maker Buy/Sell Models are full-cycle four-phase templates.

weekly_intraday_profiles.summary: Session/week profile models including TGIF Friday retracement idea.

bread_butter.summary: Symmetrical intraday model using Offset and Re-pricing engines across London, New York, London Close, and Asia sessions.

full_intraday.summary: Combines day-level session logic and delivery into a full intraday framework.

venom.summary: 2025 NY-open indices model built on a 90-minute range sweep.

source_claims: Part 3 covers trading plan/routine, risk management and position sizing, psychology/discipline/journaling, and backtesting/deliberate practice.
The book recommends mastering one model and backtesting fifty setups before moving on.
Risk, psychology, and backtesting are presented as non-optional.
engine_policy: All ICT strategies remain research_only until independently backtested.
No source-derived rule should bypass AEGIS risk policy.
Record strategy id, bias, location, draw, level, time, trigger, invalidation, target, and outcome for every test.

bias.meaning: The directional context currently favored: bullish, bearish, or unresolved.
bias.function: Sets the permitted trade direction and determines whether discount or premium locations are relevant.

location.meaning: Where current price sits inside a defined dealing range.
location.function: Filters entries to discount for bullish ideas or premium for bearish ideas.

draw.meaning: The next meaningful liquidity pool price is expected to seek.
draw.function: Defines the intended target before an entry is considered.

level.meaning: The specific price zone used for a potential entry, such as an FVG or block.
level.function: Provides an observable entry location and invalidation reference.

time.meaning: The session, killzone, macro window, or other timing context in which delivery is evaluated.
time.function: Prevents a setup from passing only on price pattern without the required time context.

trigger.meaning: The final event that confirms delivery, such as a sweep followed by MSS or CISD.
trigger.function: Converts context into a candidate setup; without it the engine passes.

liquidity.meaning: Resting orders commonly inferred around highs, lows, equal levels, and session extremes.
liquidity.function: Provides the narrative destination and the levels that may be swept or run.

market_structure.meaning: The sequence and hierarchy of confirmed swing highs and lows.
market_structure.function: Supplies directional state and structural invalidation points.

sweep.meaning: Price trades through a liquidity pool and closes back on the originating side.
sweep.function: Marks a possible rejection or reversal event, never a standalone signal.

run.meaning: Price trades through a liquidity pool and closes beyond it with continuation.
run.function: Distinguishes continuation from a sweep so the engine does not label every liquidity touch a reversal.

displacement.meaning: A forceful directional price move with materially larger body delivery than recent candles.
displacement.function: Confirms intent and qualifies nearby imbalances or structure breaks.

pd_array.meaning: A price-delivery array or zone used for rebalancing or entry context.
pd_array.function: Supplies the level step of the framework, including blocks and gaps.

entry.meaning: The price at which a paper trade would be modeled.
entry.function: Starts risk, reward, and position-size calculations; it does not place an order.

target.meaning: The modeled exit objective, normally the next aligned liquidity pool.
target.function: Defines reward and the trade's invalidation-to-objective relationship.

STH.meaning: Short-Term High, a local pivot high.
STH.function: Provides the smallest swing reference used to build intermediate and long-term structure.

ITH.meaning: Intermediate-Term High, a larger pivot assembled from short-term structure.
ITH.function: Provides a stronger structural reference than an STH.

LTH.meaning: Long-Term High, a higher-order pivot in the swing hierarchy.
LTH.function: Provides a high-timeframe liquidity and structure reference.

STL.meaning: Short-Term Low, a local pivot low.
STL.function: Provides the smallest downside swing reference.

ITL.meaning: Intermediate-Term Low, a larger pivot assembled from short-term structure.
ITL.function: Provides an intermediate downside structure reference.

LTL.meaning: Long-Term Low, a higher-order pivot in the swing hierarchy.
LTL.function: Provides a high-timeframe downside liquidity and invalidation reference.

MSS.meaning: Market Structure Shift: a displacement break of a relevant swing against the prior state.
MSS.function: Confirms a possible directional change after context; it is not a complete strategy.

CISD.meaning: Change in State of Delivery: candle-delivery evidence that price has changed directional behavior.
CISD.function: Can provide an earlier trigger than MSS and must still pass the other framework steps.

dealing_range.meaning: The selected high-to-low price range used to evaluate equilibrium and retracement.
dealing_range.function: Creates the premium, discount, and OTE reference space.

equilibrium.meaning: The 50% midpoint of a dealing range or price array.
equilibrium.function: Separates premium from discount and marks the balance reference.

premium.meaning: The half of a dealing range above equilibrium.
premium.function: Preferred location for bearish ideas and short-side PD arrays.

discount.meaning: The half of a dealing range below equilibrium.
discount.function: Preferred location for bullish ideas and long-side PD arrays.

OTE.meaning: Optimal Trade Entry retracement zone, conventionally 62% to 79% with 70.5% as a reference.
OTE.function: Refines entry location after directional bias and leg selection.

0.62-0.79 retracement.meaning: The OTE retracement interval measured against an established directional leg.
0.62-0.79 retracement.function: Rejects entries outside the configured precision-entry zone.

0.705 sweet spot.meaning: The 70.5% midpoint preference inside the OTE interval.
0.705 sweet spot.function: Ranks confluence within OTE; it is a preference, not a guarantee.

CE.meaning: Consequent Encroachment, the 50% midpoint of a gap or price array.
CE.function: Provides a precise rebalance and entry reference.

BSL.meaning: Buy-Side Liquidity, resting buy orders inferred above highs.
BSL.function: Acts as an upside draw or a level that can be swept or run.

SSL.meaning: Sell-Side Liquidity, resting sell orders inferred below lows.
SSL.function: Acts as a downside draw or a level that can be swept or run.

ERL.meaning: External Range Liquidity at the edges or outside extremes of a range.

IRL.meaning: Internal Range Liquidity inside the current dealing range, often represented by inefficiency.
IRL.function: Marks an internal rebalance objective before external liquidity.

equal highs.meaning: Two or more highs clustered within a defined tolerance.
equal highs.function: Marks a visible buy-side liquidity pool.

equal lows.meaning: Two or more lows clustered within a defined tolerance.
equal lows.function: Marks a visible sell-side liquidity pool.

PDH.function: Provides a prior-session buy-side reference and possible draw.

PDL.function: Provides a prior-session sell-side reference and possible draw.

PWH.function: Provides a higher-timeframe buy-side liquidity reference.

PWL.function: Provides a higher-timeframe sell-side liquidity reference.

OB.meaning: Order Block: the last opposing candle before a qualifying displacement move.
OB.function: Defines a candidate PD array for retest and invalidation.

breaker.meaning: A failed order block that flips role after a liquidity event and structural failure.

mitigation.meaning: A failed order block without the qualifying liquidity sweep condition.
mitigation.function: Records a weaker failed-block retest zone separately from a breaker.

rejection.meaning: A wick-based zone formed when price sweeps an extreme and rejects it.
rejection.function: Locates the rejection leg of a liquidity event.

propulsion.meaning: A block that is traded into and then followed by a launch in the block direction.
propulsion.function: Ranks a block with evidence of directional delivery.

hidden_ob.meaning: An overlapping-wick zone between two candles of the same directional color.
hidden_ob.function: Captures a less obvious PD array for research comparison.

FVG.meaning: Fair Value Gap: a three-candle price inefficiency between the first and third candle ranges.
FVG.function: Provides an imbalance entry or rebalance target when displacement qualifies it.

BISI.meaning: Buy-side Imbalance, Sell-side Inefficiency: the bullish FVG form.

SIBI.meaning: Sell-side Imbalance, Buy-side Inefficiency: the bearish FVG form.

IFVG.meaning: Inverted Fair Value Gap: an FVG invalidated through its boundary and used from the opposite side.
IFVG.function: Turns a failed imbalance into a flipped retest candidate.

implied FVG.meaning: A hidden imbalance inferred from surrounding wick relationships rather than a plain three-candle gap.
implied FVG.function: Adds a secondary inefficiency candidate for research.

BPR.meaning: Balanced Price Range: overlap between opposing imbalances.
BPR.function: Identifies a balanced overlap zone that may be revisited.

volume imbalance.meaning: A body-to-body gap where wicks may overlap.
volume imbalance.function: Captures delivery discontinuity distinct from a plain FVG.

suspension block.meaning: A candle zone suspended between two same-direction volume imbalances.
suspension block.function: Records a specialized delivery zone for comparison.

vacuum block.meaning: An opening gap beyond the prior candle's full range, often associated with a high-volatility event.
vacuum block.function: Marks a price vacuum and potential rebalance reference.

asian.meaning: The configured Asian session window in UTC unless a caller supplies market-local conversion.
asian.function: Builds the Asian range and later-session liquidity references.

london.meaning: The configured London session window in UTC.
london.function: Provides session and killzone context for delivery analysis.

new_york.meaning: The configured New York session window in UTC.
new_york.function: Provides session and killzone context for delivery analysis.

london_close.meaning: The configured London Close session window in UTC.

killzone.meaning: A predefined session window where the framework expects concentrated delivery.
killzone.function: Acts as a timing filter, not a signal by itself.

Asian range.meaning: The high-to-low range accumulated during the Asian session.
Asian range.function: Provides later-session liquidity and sweep references.

CBDR.meaning: Central Bank Dealers Range, represented locally as a configurable time-window range.
CBDR.function: Provides a bounded range for projection and session comparison.

macro.meaning: A short timing window around designated minutes near the hour or half-hour.

NDOG.meaning: New Day Opening Gap between a prior session close and the next day's opening price.
NDOG.function: Provides an opening-gap reference and possible rebalance target.

NWOG.meaning: New Week Opening Gap between the prior week and Monday opening price.

top_down.meaning: Analysis that starts on a higher timeframe and moves toward execution timeframe.
top_down.function: Prevents lower-timeframe patterns from overriding higher-timeframe context.

Daily MSS.meaning: The most recent market structure shift on the Daily timeframe.
Daily MSS.function: Supplies the base directional bias for intraday research.

SMT.meaning: Smart Money Technique divergence where correlated assets fail to confirm the same extreme.
SMT.function: Provides a confirmation or disconfirmation input, never a standalone entry.

ote.meaning: A precision retracement-entry model using OTE and PDA confluence.
ote.function: Tests whether an established leg retraces into the configured OTE zone.

order_block.meaning: A retest model built around a directional order block and displacement.
order_block.function: Tests block location, bias, retest, and lower-timeframe confirmation.

turtle_soup.meaning: A range-reversal model that fades a failed sweep of an obvious high or low.
turtle_soup.function: Tests sweep rejection, MSS/CISD confirmation, and opposite liquidity as draw.

silver_bullet.meaning: A time-based FVG scalp model constrained to designated daily windows.
silver_bullet.function: Requires a qualified imbalance inside a permitted killzone.

judas_swing.meaning: A false initial move against intended distribution before the later directional move.
judas_swing.function: Frames the manipulation leg as context rather than an entry chase.

power_of_3.function: Separates waiting, false move, and confirmed delivery phases.

accumulation.meaning: The range-building phase before a directional expansion.
accumulation.function: Defines the phase in which the engine waits for evidence.

manipulation.meaning: The false or liquidity-taking move away from the intended distribution.
manipulation.function: Identifies the move not to chase and the liquidity event to monitor.

distribution.meaning: The confirmed directional expansion after accumulation and manipulation.
distribution.function: Defines the phase where participation can be evaluated.

unicorn_smt.meaning: A confluence model combining a breaker/FVG overlap with correlated-asset divergence.
unicorn_smt.function: Requires both a price zone and SMT-style confirmation.

market_maker_models.meaning: Full-cycle buy and sell templates built from staged liquidity and delivery phases.
market_maker_models.function: Provides a research template for accumulation/manipulation/distribution sequencing.

weekly_intraday_profiles.meaning: Session and weekday delivery profiles, including the TGIF Friday retracement idea.
weekly_intraday_profiles.function: Adds calendar/session context to a directional hypothesis.

session_scalping.meaning: Short-horizon entries based on Asian range and session delivery.
session_scalping.function: Tests a session range sweep and time-constrained trigger.

low_frequency_swing.meaning: A selective one-trade or one-shot swing framework.
low_frequency_swing.function: Applies stricter setup frequency and higher-timeframe context.

bread_butter.meaning: A symmetrical intraday model using offset and re-pricing engines across sessions.
bread_butter.function: Compares session delivery templates without enabling live execution.

full_intraday.meaning: A complete day-level framework combining session logic and price delivery.
full_intraday.function: Requires context, time, liquidity, level, and trigger evidence.

venom.meaning: A NY-open indices model centered on a 90-minute range sweep.
venom.function: Tests a defined opening range and subsequent liquidity event.

advanced_pd_arrays.meaning: A collection of specialized imbalance and reversal concepts.
advanced_pd_arrays.function: Keeps advanced arrays classified for research without treating names as proof.

1st Presented FVG.meaning: The first qualifying fair value gap presented after a selected delivery event.
1st Presented FVG.function: Ranks the earliest imbalance candidate in an advanced-array study.

IOFED.meaning: Implied Order Flow Entry Detection, a specialized delivery/entry concept from the source material.
IOFED.function: Stores an advanced entry label for later validation rather than inventing certainty.

Reaper IFVG.function: Keeps the variation distinct from the base IFVG detector for research.

Enigma FVG.function: Preserves the source label while requiring separate validation before promotion.

Reversal Sequence.meaning: A sequence describing liquidity event, delivery change, and reversal confirmation.

research_only.meaning: An output that may be analyzed or paper-tested but is not authorized for live execution.
research_only.function: Enforces the Trading agent's safety boundary.

invalidation.meaning: The price condition that proves the setup premise is no longer valid.
invalidation.function: Defines the modeled stop and prevents narrative override.

position sizing.meaning: Calculating quantity from account risk and stop distance.
position sizing.function: Limits paper exposure through the existing RiskEngine.

backtesting.meaning: Running a defined model over historical candles with recorded outcomes.
backtesting.function: Tests repeatability before a strategy can be considered for promotion.

deliberate practice.meaning: Repeated, logged review of a single model and its execution conditions.
deliberate practice.function: Supports the source recommendation to master and validate one model before expanding.

journal.meaning: A structured record of setup context, decision, risk, and outcome.
journal.function: Preserves evidence for review and change detection.
